names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 15 Μαρτίου, «Άγιος Αγάπιος και των συν αυτώ μάρτυρες: Πλήσιος, Ρωμύλος, Τιμόλαος, Αλέξανδρος, Αλέξανδρος (έτερος), Διονύσιος καί Διονύσιος (έτερος)», with the rank words left off.

Read out of the Ohrid Prologue's first heading for the Julian 15 March on pravoslavno.rs, „Свети мученик Агапије и седморица с њим: Публије, Тимолај, Ромил, два Александра и два Дионисија.“, where it is the fourth name the heading prints. The rank words Свети мученик stand at the head of the whole company and are left off, and the heading gives this man no epithet and no city, so the bare forename is what the source gives.

Read out of the name link behind days.pravoslavie.ru's line for 15 марта ст. ст., «Ромил Кесарийский (Палестинский), мч.», with the rank word left off. The day line itself declines the name and gives no epithet.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 15 марта ст. ст. — «Мч. Агапия и с ним семи мучеников: Пуплия, Тимолая, Ромила, двух Александров и двух Дионисиев (I, II) (303).»

attestations.note: The line is one line for the eight and this folder is one of them; it enumerates them, so it is eight rows and not one. The year it closes with, 303, is the year the Ohrid Prologue also gives and which this folder already records as falling inside the reign of Diocletian; it is not written over the interval. The life page behind the line, life646, puts the suffering at Caesarea in Palestine under that reign, which it dates 284 to 305. The day page prints no hymn for any of the eight.
Not checked: doxologia.ro's calendar for the same civil day (30 September 2026).

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 15ης Μαρτίου — «Άγιος Αγάπιος και των συν αυτώ μάρτυρες: Πλήσιος, Ρωμύλος, Τιμόλαος, Αλέξανδρος, Αλέξανδρος (έτερος), Διονύσιος καί Διονύσιος (έτερος)»

attestations.note: The page enumerates the eight and gives each his country: «Ο Αγάπιος ήταν από τη Γάζα της Παλαιστίνης, ο Τιμόλαος από τη Μαύρη Θάλασσα, οι δύο Διονύσιοι από την Τρίπολη της Φοινίκης, ο Ρωμύλος -υποδιάκονος- από τη Λύδδα ή Διόσπολη, ο Πλήσιος και οι δύο Αλέξανδροι από την Αίγυπτο». It puts the martyrdom in the persecution of Diocletian «(284-304)» — the corpus's interval, 284–305, comes from doxologia and stands — before Urbanus, the eparch of Caesarea, and says they all died by beheading. It prints two distichs and an apolytikion that name them. The page makes him a subdeacon and puts his home at Lydda, or Diospolis, and the distich it keeps for Plesius has him beheaded with three others.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 28.03.2026 (15. март ст. ст.) — „Свети мученик Агапије и седморица с њим: Публије, Тимолај, Ромил, два Александра и два Дионисија.“

attestations.note: The day's first entry, an enumerated company of eight: the heading names Agapius and then the seven with him, „Публије, Тимолај, Ромил, два Александра и два Дионисија“. It is the same company the Greek and the Romanian already keep in this folder — Caesarea in Palestine, the prince Urban, Diocletian's persecution, eight men, all beheaded — and the Greek line already quoted here names the same seven beside Agapius in the same order but for the first. The Prologue dates the beheading 303, which falls inside the reign this folder already holds; a sourced interval is not narrowed on a reading, so no date was touched. Its own reading of the seven is unlike either other page: it makes them not yet Christians and never baptised with water, baptised instead in their blood, where doxologia makes them six young men already confessing and saint.gr gives each of them a country. That is recorded in the life and not reconciled. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion.

death.note: saint.gr: «Έζησαν και κέρδισαν τα αθάνατα βραβεία, κατά το διωγμό του Διοκλητιανού (284-304) εναντίον της Εκκλησίας». The page gives no year, so the interval is the reign as it prints it; the three folders the corpus already held carry doxologia's 284–305 and are left as they are.
